title: Sequence-aware traffic scheduler prototype for staged rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and prototype a 'sequence-aware' traffic scheduler surface for the Redwood Console that lets operators compose staged rollouts as ordered cohorts with dependency rules, gating conditions, and automatic rollback targets. Goals: (1) allow product/ops teams to express ordered migrations (A -> B -> C) where cohorts can be defined by user attributes, region, model variant, or custom predicates; (2) visualize timeline + expected ramp curves with preflight simulation; (3) expose guardrails (abort conditions, SLO thresholds) and one-click rollback hooks; (4) integrate with existing rollout simulation and the Console's decision panel so on-call can rehearse and run incident drills.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas UI where a user can create a sequence of 2..10 cohorts and reorder them interactively
Ability to assign cohort definitions (percent, attribute filter, region, model tag) and to set per-step duration and ramp curve
Visual timeline showing expected traffic distribution over time plus an overlay of selected metric thresholds (latency, error rate, cost burn)
Simulation mode that runs a dry-run and surfaces estimated token-cost delta and KV cache warmup risk
Rollback / abort control visible on each step with pre-filled recommended actions based on thresholds
Prototype reviewed by PM and two backend engineers and updated to reflect scheduling granularity constraints
design_notes: Core interaction pattern: drag-and-drop sequenced lanes + inline edit card for cohort details
Prefer 'preset' ramp profiles (immediate, linear, sigmoid) to limit cognitive load; allow custom for advanced users
Expose a 'safety score' computed from selected metrics and cohort size to guide defaults
Show dependency badges (e.g., 'requires KV-warm' or 'data-migration lock') when cohort uses model variants with known cold-starts
Trade-off: too many inline settings increases clutter — we default to minimal card view with an 'advanced' flyout
Mobile / narrow viewport behavior: stack sequence vertically with condensed timeline
